title: 90785 CPT Code: When to Bill Interactive Complexity (2026)
summary: 90785 CPT code for interactive complexity: the four factors, which codes it pairs with, what Medicare pays in 2026, and why interpreters no longer count.
body_markdown:
The 90785 CPT code is the add-on for interactive complexity. You add it to an evaluation or a psychotherapy session when the way people in the room communicated made the work harder. Think of a parent who keeps contradicting the history, a disclosure of abuse you now have to report, a child who can only show you what happened with toys.


It is never billed alone, and in 2026 Medicare pays USD 14.70 for it nationally at the non facility rate (USD 11.69 at the facility rate). The rules changed in 2022, when interpreters stopped counting as a reason to bill it. Plenty of guides still say they do.

## What is the 90785 CPT code?


The CPT descriptor reads "Interactive complexity (List separately in addition to the code for primary procedure)." The[Medicare contractor billing guide for LCD L34616](https://downloads.cms.gov/medicare-coverage-database/lcd_attachments/34616_20/L34616_PSYCH014_BCG.pdf) puts it plainly: it "refers to communication difficulties during the psychiatric procedure," and add-on codes "may only be reported in conjunction with other codes, never alone."


Two things trip people up. It does not add time; the[American Psychiatric Association sheet on the code](https://www.psychiatry.org/getmedia/86779486-e341-4793-81b0-3f065f2c914c/APA-AACP-CPT-Interactive-Complexity.pdf) says it "does not change the time for the psychotherapy service." And it is not a difficult-patient code. Something specific has to happen in that session.


### 90785 at a glance


90785


Type Add-on (ZZZ in the 2026 Medicare file)


2026 Medicare, national USD 14.70 non facility, USD 11.69 facility


Pairs with 90791, 90792, 90832, 90834, 90837, 90833, 90836, 90838, 90853


Never with 90839/90840, 90846/90847, or an E/M visit on its own


Telehealth On the CY 2026 Medicare telehealth list


## When can you bill 90785?


When at least one of four things happens during the visit and your note says so.[APA Services](https://www.apaservices.org/practice/reimbursement/health-codes/2022-reporting-interactive-complexity) lists them like this:


1. **Maladaptive communication.** High anxiety, high reactivity, repeated questions or disagreement among the people in the session gets in the way of care.
2. **Caregiver emotions or behavior.** A parent or caregiver's reaction gets in the way of them understanding or helping with the treatment plan.
3. **A sentinel event and a mandated report.** Abuse or neglect comes out, you have to report it to a third party, and you start that conversation with the patient and others present.
4. **Play equipment or devices.** The patient has not developed, or has lost, the language to communicate the usual way, so you use toys, devices or other tools to get through.


The contractor guide says these factors typically come up with patients who have a guardian or bring family into the session. They also come up when a school, a probation officer or child welfare is involved. The APA sheet says it is common with children and teenagers but "may apply to visits by adults, as well."


### When a session does not qualify


A hard session is not enough. These do not support 90785 on their own:


- A parent or partner is in the room and everyone communicates without trouble.
- The patient came alone and nothing was disclosed.
- The session ran long. Time goes in the psychotherapy code.
- The patient is difficult in general. APA Services warns against billing it for every session with a difficult patient.
- An interpreter joined. More on that below.


## What codes can 90785 be billed with?


It goes on the diagnostic evaluations (90791, 90792) and the individual psychotherapy codes (90832, 90834, 90837). It also goes on the psychotherapy add-ons used with a medical visit (90833, 90836, 90838) and on group psychotherapy (90853). Both APA sources agree on that list.


It does not go with crisis psychotherapy (90839, 90840), family psychotherapy (90846, 90847), psychological or neuropsychological testing, or adaptive behavior services. The 2012 APA sheet also rules out 90849, multiple family group therapy. The 2022 guidance does not mention it, so check with the payer before you pair them.


### Can you add 90785 to 99214?


Only when the visit also includes psychotherapy. Billed as 99214 alone, no. Billed as 99214 plus 90833, yes. The 90785 attaches to the psychotherapy part of the visit. APA Services says interactive complexity "is not applicable to an evaluation and management (E/M) service alone."


## How much does 90785 pay in 2026?


Medicare pays USD 14.70 nationally at the non facility rate and USD 11.69 at the facility rate. That is 0.44 and 0.35 relative value units times the 2026 conversion factor of 33.4009, from the[CMS relative value file](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/payment/fee-schedules/physician/pfs-relative-value-files) . Your contractor's local amount is what actually pays, and Medicaid and commercial plans set their own rates.


Here is what the add-on does to a few typical claims:


Claim Without 90785 With 90785


90791, diagnostic evaluation USD 173.35 USD 188.05


90834, psychotherapy, 45 min USD 113.90 USD 128.59


90837, psychotherapy, 60 min USD 167.00 USD 181.70


90853, group psychotherapy USD 30.39 USD 45.09


99214 + 90833 USD 217.11 USD 231.80


2026 Medicare national amounts, non facility, before locality adjustment. 90785 is also on the[CY 2026 Medicare telehealth list](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/coverage/telehealth/list-services) , so the same pairing works by video.


## Can you bill 90785 for an interpreter?


Not on its own. In 2022 the CPT guidance dropped "interpreters" and "language translators" from the interactive complexity rules, to line up with federal and CMS language ([APA Services](https://www.apaservices.org/practice/reimbursement/health-codes/2022-reporting-interactive-complexity) ). The APA sheet quotes CMS: "90785 generally should not be billed solely for the purpose of translation or interpretation services."


The older wording is still around. The Medicare contractor guide attached to LCD L34616, last revised in 2016, still lists interpreters, and so do some pages that rank for this code today. If an interpreter was present and one of the four factors also happened, bill on the factor and document that.


## How do you bill 90785 with group therapy?


Per patient. APA Services says it can be reported with 90853 "for a specified patient when group psychotherapy includes interactive complexity" and "should not be reported for every patient participating in the group service." Put it on the claim of the member it applied to, and write the factor in that member's note.


## How should you document 90785?


The note has to show two things: what got in the way, and what it did to the session. "90785 due to communication barriers" will not hold up. Something like this will:


*Example: Both parents attended. Each repeatedly disputed the other's account of the child's sleep and school problems, and the father interrupted the child's answers several times. I redirected four times to get the child's own account, which limited the time left for skills practice.*


For the other factors, write down:


- For a sentinel event: what was disclosed, who you reported it to, and that you discussed the report with the patient and others present.
- For play or devices: what you used and why ordinary conversation was not possible.
- For caregiver behavior: what the caregiver did and how it affected the treatment plan.
- The psychotherapy time, for the primary code. 90785 adds none.


APA Services gives worked examples: divorced parents who keep challenging each other (90834 with 90785), and an older patient whose daughter discloses elder abuse during the session (90837 with 90785). Our guide to[psychotherapy notes](https://www.mdhub.ai/blog-posts/psychotherapy-notes) covers the rest of the note.


## Why do 90785 claims get denied?


These are the pairings that get 90785 denied. Set them as edits in your billing system, or check them by hand before claims go out:


What went out Fix


90785 with no primary code Bill it on the same claim as 90791, 90792, 90832 to 90838 or 90853


90785 with 90839 or 90840 Crisis sessions take 90839 and 90840 only


90785 with an E/M visit and no psychotherapy add-on Add it only when 90833, 90836 or 90838 is billed


90785 with 90846 or 90847 Not allowed with family psychotherapy


90785 on every member of a group Only the member the factor applied to


90785 set as a default for a patient Decide visit by visit


More on working denials in our guides to[denial management](https://www.mdhub.ai/blog-posts/denial-management) and[claim scrubbing](https://www.mdhub.ai/blog-posts/claim-scrubbing) .

## 90785 CPT code FAQ


What is the 90785 CPT code?


The add-on code for interactive complexity: a communication factor during an evaluation or psychotherapy session that made the service harder to deliver. It is never billed alone.


What codes can 90785 be billed with?


90791, 90792, 90832, 90834, 90837, the add-ons 90833, 90836 and 90838, and 90853 group therapy.


Can 90785 be added to 99214?


Only when the visit is billed with a psychotherapy add-on such as 90833. Not with 99214 alone.


Can 90837 and 90785 be billed together?


Yes, when one of the four factors happened and is documented. 90785 does not change the time.


Can 90785 be billed with 90839?


No. It cannot be reported with crisis psychotherapy, 90839 or 90840.


How much does 90785 pay?


In 2026 Medicare pays USD 14.70 nationally at the non facility rate and USD 11.69 at the facility rate, before locality adjustment.


Can 90785 be used for an interpreter?


Not on its own. The 2022 CPT guidance removed interpreters and translators as a reason to bill it.


Can 90785 be billed for every patient in a group?


No. Only for the member the factor applied to.
